newsitem.title: UK: Gas oil, gasoline firm in Med, fuel oil weaker.
newsitem.headline: Gas oil, gasoline firm in Med, fuel oil weaker.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday with light ends and middle distillates boosted by local and Asian demand while fuel oil slipped as buying talk disappeared.

Gas oil remained strong, backed mainly by Asian demand since local interest was only moderate. Some sellers of Italian 0.2 percent were holding out for high fob quotes +$4 whereas buying interest was probably $1 lower. Fob barrels were almost non-existant except in small 20-22kt parcels.
Demand for Russian was still strong and high fob quotes +$4 was considered realistic.
Gasoline was steady in a tightish market as Italian players geared up for increased demand ahead of two long weekends at the end of April and the start of May after a series of turnarounds.
"I think most people had covered themselves pretty well at least until the middle of April because of the turnaround season, but now they're going to start needing material," one trader said.
Traders said there were also small pockets of demand out the Eastern Mediterranean.
Naphtha lifted slightly off lower levels seen late on Thursday mainly on crude in an otherwise quiet market.
Fuel oil was a touch lower as demand for high sulphur appeared to evaporate. Traders said early week pricing plays were finished and the market was finding a more normal level.
High sulphur supply looked firmer, with an Italian refiner delaying maintenance to profit from healthy margins and said to have 20-30,000 tonnes of fuel oil to market next week.
Lower Med swaps, at around $76 for May, also pointed to a downward trend, traders said.
Low sulphur was again tranquil, though the big Italian end-user was heard to have bought quietly, with at least one northern European cargo picked up on a quotes related basis.
